title: Malana Travel Guide - The Ancient Village of Himachal, Off Beat Destination
content:
Malana - Himachal Pradesh,

Tucked away deep in the Parvati Valley of Himachal Pradesh, at around 2,600 meters above sea level, lies Malana, a village that has intrigued travelers for centuries. It’s not just another mountain village - it’s a place wrapped in mystery, culture, and age-old traditions that make it unlike anywhere else in India.

Reaching Malana feels like stepping into another world. To get here, you travel through the winding mountain roads of Kasol and Jari, and then take a short but steep trek from Malana Gate. As you climb up, the views keep opening up - rolling pine forests, the sparkling Malana River below, and snow-covered peaks of the Chandrakhani and Deo Tibba ranges in the distance. The journey itself feels like an adventure, and by the time you reach the village, you realize you’re about to witness something very unique.

Malana is often called the “Little Greece of India,” as locals believe they are descendants of Alexander the Great’s soldiers. The village has its own rules, its own language (Kanashi), and even its own system of governance, which is considered one of the oldest democracies in the world. Outsiders are not allowed to touch houses, temples, or even the locals themselves. If you accidentally break a rule, you’re expected to pay a fine. While these customs may seem unusual to visitors, they are part of what makes Malana so special - it has preserved its identity for hundreds of years, even while the world around it keeps changing.

But Malana is not only about its culture; it’s also about the breathtaking natural beauty that surrounds it. The village sits in a bowl-shaped valley, framed by towering mountains and dense forests. Trekkers and photographers love this place for its untouched landscapes, and many travelers come here to simply disconnect and enjoy peace. From Malana, you can also embark on the Chandrakhani Pass trek, which is one of the most scenic trails in Himachal.

Malana is also globally known for something else - its famous Malana Cream, a type of hashish that has gained a reputation across the world. While this attracts a lot of curiosity, travelers must remember that the use of cannabis is illegal in India, and getting into trouble here can ruin the trip. It’s always better to focus on the beauty, the treks, and the incredible culture that the village offers.

A trip to Malana is not for everyone. The rules can feel strict, and the trek might be tiring. But if you’re someone who loves exploring hidden places, learning about ancient traditions, and being surrounded by raw Himalayan beauty, Malana will leave you with stories you’ll never forget.

How to Reach Malana:

  • Drive up to Jari (23 km from Kasol). From there, take a cab to Malana Gate and trek 4 km uphill to the village.
  • Nearest Airport: Bhuntar Airport (35 km from Kasol).
  • Nearest Train Station: Joginder Nagar or Chandigarh.
  • Stay Options: No hotels inside the village, but guesthouses and homestays are available near Malana Gate and in Jari.

Best Time to Visit Malana:

  • March - June (Peak Season): Pleasant weather, best for trekking.
  • September - November (Moderate): Clear skies, ideal for photography.
  • December - February (Winter): Heavy snow, trek can be difficult but views are magical.
  • July - August (Low Season): Monsoon makes the trail slippery - avoid if possible.

Distances from Key Cities:

  • Malana to Kasol: 23 km
  • Malana to Kullu: 45 km
  • Malana to Manali: 85 km
  • Malana to Shimla: 240 km
  • Malana to Delhi: 520 km (approx. 12–13 hrs by road)

Things to Do in Malana:

  • Explore the Village Culture - Learn about unique customs and traditions.
  • Trek to Chandrakhani Pass - Scenic route with breathtaking Himalayan views.
  • Photography - Capture wooden houses, landscapes, and snow peaks.
  • Visit the Malana River - Peaceful spot for relaxation and walks.
  • Try Local Food - Himachali dishes available at homestays outside the main village.
  • Disconnect from the World - No network, no distractions - just nature and peace.

Top 5 Places to Visit Near Malana (within 50 km):

1- Kasol (23 km) - The backpacker’s paradise.

2- Tosh (45 km) - Famous for its views and hippie vibe.

3- Kheerganga (35 km) - Trek with hot water springs.

4- Manikaran Sahib (28 km) - Sikh Gurudwara with hot springs.

5- Chalal Village (25 km) - Riverside village near Kasol.
